stories.body: Climate negotiations in Antalya stretched into Sunday after a draft agreement removed all references to fossil fuels, prompting resistance from the EU and vulnerable countries. Saudi Arabia and other producers had opposed an earlier call for a faster phase-out. COP31 President Murat Kurum presented a last-minute compromise, saying it addressed concerns about fossil fuels and adaptation funding, but approval remained pending. Other disputes concern carbon capture, electricity generation and the removal of a proposed $120 billion adaptation funding target.
stories.headline: COP31 enters second day of overtime over fossil fuels and climate finance

stories.body: Countries meeting in Geneva failed to agree on a mandate for a legally binding treaty governing autonomous weapons after overnight negotiations ran into Russian objections. The consensus-based forum instead adopted a weaker commitment to continue negotiations toward an agreement by 2028, without guaranteeing binding rules. More than 100 states had pushed for new law, while the US and several other military technology powers resisted binding obligations. Humanitarian groups warned that weapons development is outpacing efforts to establish human control and accountability.
stories.headline: UN talks fail to secure binding negotiations on autonomous weapons

stories.body: Bahrain said an Iranian attack caused a fire and material damage at an unnamed civilian industrial facility late Saturday, with no injuries initially reported. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it had targeted US military positions at two bases in Bahrain in response to alleged violations of Iranian airspace. Its claim to have destroyed US air-defense radars was not independently established in the supplied report. Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, has faced repeated attacks during the US-Israel war with Iran.
stories.headline: Bahrain reports Iranian attack caused fire at civilian industrial facility

stories.body: The Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire after a drone attack in the Gulf of Finland and drifted into Finnish territorial waters. Its crew was evacuated, and Finnish authorities reported no detected environmental damage or danger to other shipping. The sanctioned vessel, bound for Kaliningrad, is operated by a company linked to Russia's military. Finnish defense forces said Ukraine was likely responsible, but Kyiv had not commented. Finland also reported a suspected Russian helicopter airspace violation potentially connected to the response.
stories.headline: Drone strike sets Russian cargo ship ablaze near Finland

stories.body: Mexican special forces captured alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, in Guasave, Sinaloa, during an operation that killed four soldiers and seven alleged gunmen. The raid, supported by US intelligence according to Mexico's defense ministry, triggered hours of fighting, burning roadblocks and panic at a baseball game. Meza Flores, one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives, was flown to Mexico City with two alleged associates. Experts warned that his removal could intensify existing cartel power struggles.
stories.headline: Mexico captures El Chapo Isidro in operation that kills 11

stories.body: The EU and Indonesia signed a trade agreement after ten years of negotiations, providing for the removal of 98.5% of tariffs between the two economies. The agreement would improve European access to Indonesia's market of 280 million people and supplies of nickel used in batteries, while easing Indonesian exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear. The signing comes shortly before Indonesia's existing EU trade preferences expire on January 1; the supplied report does not establish when the new tariff arrangements take effect.
stories.headline: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal covering almost all tariffs

stories.body: The FBI is reportedly investigating a suspected breach of the National Crime Information Center, which law enforcement agencies use to share sensitive information including warrants, missing-person records and stolen property. US media cited people briefed on the incident, and President Trump acknowledged the reports, but the FBI had not publicly detailed the scope or impact. The incident follows a separate suspected theft of FBI employee information earlier this year. An apparent attack on an Agriculture Department payment system was also reported, with no established connection between the incidents.
stories.headline: FBI investigates suspected breach of national crime database

stories.body: Two polls project a clear parliamentary majority for the PP and Vox, while differing substantially on the gap between the PP and PSOE. Ipsos for La Vanguardia puts the PP at 30.3% and PSOE at 29.8%, with the right-wing bloc averaging about 190 seats. Sigma Dos for El Mundo gives the PP 31.5%, PSOE 28% and Vox 18.3%, translating into 183–194 seats for PP and Vox combined, above the 176 needed for a majority. Both indicate that the PP would need Vox to govern and that fragmentation is weakening parties to PSOE's left.
stories.headline: Polls project PP-Vox majority ahead of November 29 election

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez said Tuesday's cabinet meeting would approve extending the extraordinary bank tax through 2027, with the government expecting €1.4 billion in revenue earmarked by law for housing. The announced uses include protected housing construction, renovation and tax relief for tenants. The government estimates the proceeds could support more than 6,000 affordable homes, renovations to as many as 52,000 properties and tax relief for nearly 120,000 tenants over the next parliamentary term. The extension is an announced measure awaiting approval, made a week before the general election.
stories.headline: Sánchez proposes extending bank tax through 2027 to fund housing

stories.body: A technical failure at Iberdrola's hydrogen plant in the Zona Franca has sidelined 23 TMB buses, particularly affecting the X1, V19 and D20 routes. TMB says overall service has fallen by 2.5–3.8%, with some scheduled gaps increasing from seven to nine minutes, and expects supplies to recover within weeks. Unions dispute that assessment and warn disruption could last until February. They say the shortage is compounded by buses being diverted to replacement service for the L2 metro closure between La Pau and Gorg, scheduled to continue through December 3.
stories.headline: Hydrogen supply failure reduces service on Barcelona's X1, V19 and D20 buses
